title: provider-auth: the directory-key alternative names the wrong provider's certificate
description:
draft-atwood-mimi-provider-auth.md, the "Keys could also be published in
the directory document instead of DNS" bullet near line 749. Verified
2026-11-26, not just suspected.

## The text

  That would rest their trust on the target's TLS server certificate,
  which is to say on the Web PKI [...]

## Why it is wrong

The draft's own model has the SOURCE provider publish its key under its
own domain and the target fetch it to verify a signed request:

- L116: "publishes a public key in DNS under its own domain and signs
  each [request]"
- L273 table: "DNS keys | RFC 9421 request signature | DNS, under the
  source domain"

So a directory document carrying those keys would be the source's
directory, fetched by the target. The trust would rest on the SOURCE's
TLS server certificate. "The target's" has the direction backwards.

## The fix

Replace "the target's TLS server certificate" with "the source
provider's TLS server certificate". The rest of the bullet, including
the Web PKI argument, stands: the point is that a directory-published
key inherits Web PKI trust, and that is true whichever provider serves
it.

Worth a sweep of the neighbouring Security Considerations bullets for
the same source/target inversion while the file is open.
